ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a circle with V as the center, Q and S at the left and right ends of the horizontal diameter, and the problem gives that QS is a diameter. R is above the circle, radius VR is vertically upward, radius VS is horizontally to the right, and a right angle is marked between VR and VS. T is at the lower right of the circle, and the central angle between radius VT and VS is labeled 75°. Reasoning: Need to find m\widehat{QRT}, that is, the arc starting from Q and passing through R to T, which along the circumference successively contains arcs QR, RS, ST. Because QS is a diameter, the upper semicircular arc from Q through R to S is 180°. Also because central angle RVS is a right angle, arc RS = 90°, therefore arc QR = 180° - 90° = 90°. Central angle SVT = 75°, so arc ST = 75°. Therefore m\widehat{QRT} = 90° + 90° + 75° = 255°.

raw_record.question_text: $\overline{QS}$ is a diameter of $\odot V$. Find $m\widehat{QRT}$.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: circle centered at V has horizontal diameter QS; radii VR and VS form a marked right angle, and radii VS and VT form a central angle of 75°. The target arc QRT is the arc starting at Q, passing through R, and ending at T, so it is made of arcs QR, RS, and ST. From the text, use that QS is a diameter, so the upper semicircle from Q through R to S measures 180°. Alternatively, the right angle shows arc RS = 90°, making arc QR = 90° on that semicircle. The central angle SVT = 75° gives arc ST = 75°. Therefore m arc QRT = arc QR + arc RS + arc ST = 90 + 90 + 75 = 255.
